narrative.summaryIntro:
Kashi Vishwanath Temple, located in the sacred city of Varanasi on the banks of the Ganges, is one of the most important pilgrimage sites in Hinduism. The temple is dedicated to Shiva, known here as Vishwanath (Lord of Benares), and is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas—the holiest shrines dedicated to Shiva.

The present structure was rebuilt in the 18th century by Rani Ahilya Bai Holkar of Indore. The temple's golden spire is an iconic symbol of Varanasi and stands as a testament to centuries of spiritual devotion. Millions of pilgrims visit annually seeking blessings and liberation (moksha).
